provenance: PR #66 R2. The PRICE of ADR-036, measured instead of asserted. Its Consequences bullet said a main-document click whose only effect is inside a frame can no longer verify itself with `text_visible`, and then said `No committed case authored that shape` — a limitation declared in prose that no suite could go red on, which is the shape this repo has been burned by three times. The fixture was already in the tree: `frames-swap.html` is a main-document button whose only effect is the iframe's `srcdoc`, and the one case on it (`replan-after-an-iframe-only-change-is-not-laundering`) asserts `Filing loaded`, a string absent on BOTH settings, so it cannot discriminate. This case names the FRAME's own text, `Document ID:`, and pins the whole ruling in one trace: step 2's click resolves in the main document (`resolved.scope` = frames-swap.html), `page_changed` is true because the frame really did change, and `postcondition_ok` is FALSE anyway — the action worked and its postcondition cannot see it. Then it pins the declared way out, the `wait_for` carve-out: the replan's page-wide `wait_for` reads the frame, goes true, and the `extract` resolves in `about:srcdoc`. Watched against the pre-ADR-036 mechanism (`check_state(..., scope=None)` everywhere, one line at the call site) it is red on four checks at once: `checks {"status": true, "verdict": true, "recovery": false, "replans": false, "trace_postconditions": false, "resolved_scopes": false}`, `got {"status": "success", "answer": "NIMBUS-10K-2025", "reason": null}` — page-wide, the click's postcondition is satisfied by the frame, so there is no failure, no replan and no recovery at all. That difference IS the trade-off: one extra replan on a legitimate frame-effect click, which is the cost this ADR pays for refusing a decoy document's `postcondition_ok: true`.

triage.note: the cost side of ADR-036's ruling, and the pin on its `wait_for` carve-out being a real recovery path rather than a sentence
